title: Create new upload account in Akamai Netstorage
content:
Note: Creating a new upload account for an “Add on Application” is done by Akamai Control Center Administrators for AoA CP code.

1. About Team and Personal Accounts

The team upload account is used for generic access, such as GitHub workflows, Azure pipelines, and other services.

The name of the upload account should be the same as the name of the team, followed by “nonprd” for non-production/test accounts, and “prd” for production accounts:

  • {DEXF consumer id}_nonprd

  • {DEXF Consumer id}_prd

DEXF Consumer Id is registered by the experience team via https://i-p-e-x.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/5 .

When a team account is created a personal account should also be created for the PO and/or DevOps lead in that team. This is because that person should be able to authenticate and fully access the directories used by the team and services.

Personal accounts should be named according to that person’s IKEA acronym/network ID. A personal account should have access to both non-production and production subdirectories (current and legacy NetStorage area names are equal to CP codes). Do not create two personal for this separation. Also note that personal accounts - unless it is a personal account for one of our own DevOps team members - must have subdirectory restrictions, so that they cannot see other teams' data and directory contents.

2. Akamai Secrets and Credentials - Naming Conventions

Below is our recommendation for naming the Akamai secrets and credentials that is used in this guide:

  • Storage Group Name: add as Azure Key Vault secret “AkamaiStorageGroupName”

  • HTTP Domain Name: add as Azure Key Vault secret “AkamaiStorageHttpDomainName”

  • Upload Account ID: add as Azure Key Vault secret “AkamaiStorageId”

  • HTTP API key: add as Azure Key Vault secret “AkamaiStorageHttpApiKey”

  • SSH Public Key: add as Azure Key Vault secret “AkamaiStorageSSHPublicKey”

  • SSH Private Key: add as Azure Key Vault secret “AkamaiStorageSSHPrivateKey”

3. Determine Upload Account E-mail

Use existing team “operations” e-mail; i.e., <team>-operations@inter.ikea.com for those team that have such an address. If the team does not have that type of e-mail then Create an Office 365 Group and related MS Team.

4. Determine Root Directory Availability

Each team must have a root directory. The name of the directory should be the same as the name of the team. I.e., {experience }.

Root directories cannot be created within Akamai control center; they need to be created manually, which can be done using WinSCP - see https://i-p-e-x.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/IPEX/pages/5921866015/Working+with+Akamai+NetStorage#WinSCP - or using a remote SSH command (mkdir). A subdirectory restriction (see below) does not imply that the directory gets created if it does not exist.

5. Check if Serve from Zip is Desired

Upload accounts can use the feature Serve from Zip. This is currently the recommended approach, particularly if each upload is large containing many files. Discuss this topic with the PO or the DevOps lead.

It’s also possible to enable this feature later.

6. Determine Azure Key Vault Availability and Accessibility

Since SSH keys will be used for authentication they should be stored in Azure Key Vaults. Ideally the keys that belong to non-production should be stored in the team’s non-production key vault; production SSH keys should be stored in the production key vault. If the team only has one key vault then the name of the SSH keys need to be clear to make a separation between production and non-production. See our naming conventions in section 2. Also make sure you have personal access to the team’s key vault(s) so that you can add the keys once generated.

7. Generate the SSH Keys

For team upload accounts no password is required. For personal accounts a password should be used. The PO/DevOps lead can send the personal public SSH key via MS Teams.

Use ssh-keygen to generate the keys; I.e., ssh-keygen -v -t rsa -b 2048 -C "{experiece name}_{environment}" -f {experiece name}_{environment}.

For example:

  • ssh-keygen -v -t rsa -b 2048 -C "kombinera_nonprd" -f kombinera_nonprd

  • ssh-keygen -v -t rsa -b 2048 -C "kombinera_prd" -f kombinera_prd

8. Add Upload Account

Log in to Akamai Control center and choose NetStorage in menu

In menu alternative upload account choose “Add Upload Account” and enter account details as described in section 1 above.

Primary and secondary contacts can be anyone of the Akamai administrators.

Proceed by associating new upload account with main/root upload directory. Test accounts should be added below directory 809385 and production accounts below 809386.

Continue by expanding the main/root upload directory and create the subdirectory restriction for the new upload account.

Note: all new folders should be created below addon-app i.e. a restriction for “experience” for test environment should be added as a subdirectory restriction for /809385/addon-app/{DEXF Id}.

DEXF Consumer Id is registered by the experience team via https://i-p-e-x.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/5 .

Finally make sure that Read-Write access is set for account and then hit next:

Once subdirectory restrictions are set add the public SSH key generated in section 7.

Optionally (not for RSync) enable access to upload account via CLI / HTTP API. Ask team contact persons to generate and add to Azure Key Vault. Recommended way is to use Rsync which use ssh key to authenticate, see below.

If you want to access account via File Manager (not recommended since tool is not good) you need to enable this.

Save created API key and hit next.

Optionally enable Serve from Zip as described in section 5:

In last step review then hit create. Note: If using Google Chrome the review step may sometimes be stuck - it is possible to continue with creation despite that this step is hanging.

New upload account is now visible in list of accounts. Note that it will take up to 2 hours to propagate.

9. Verify Upload Account

Once the upload account has been propagated, use the private SSH key generated to verify the upload account. It should be possible to successfully logon using e.g. WinSCP. Also make sure that the subdirectory restrictions are in place.

If a personal account has been created for a PO/DevOps lead ask the person to check his/her upload account using the SSH key, and confirm that correct visibility is in place (subdirectory restrictions). A PO/DevOps lead for a particular team should not be able to see other teams' upload account directories.

10. Upload the SSH keys to Team Azure Key Vaults

Once the SSH keys have been created and verified it is time to upload them to Azure Key Vault. One way of doing that is to Use Azure CLI to upload pertinent secrets below to Azure Key Vault. Follow the naming conventions as described in section 2, unless there is a need for another naming standard.

11. Request Akamai Property Change

By default the directories created for the upload accounts point to the “old” Akamai NetStorage area. To be able to use the newly created account Akamai needs to make a property change.

The old Akamai area is briefly described here. Property changes are fully described here. Finally, if the team is already using old Akamai and plan to move to the new area, a migration guide exists that covers the essential steps for that.

12. Enable SSH Key Rotation

Once the team and upload accounts are in use in production it is recommended they setup automatic SSH key rotation, which is implemented here.
